title: How Ultrasonic Sensors Work | HC-SR04 Explained in 3D (Arduino Distance Sensor)
description:
How does an ultrasonic sensor measure distance using nothing but sound? This 3D animated explainer takes the HC-SR04 apart step by step: the physics of ultrasound, the piezoelectric transducers inside, the 4-step measurement, the distance formula, the Arduino code, and the sensor's blind spots.

⏱ CHAPTERS
0:00 Intro: seeing with sound
0:20 What is ultrasound?
0:37 Anatomy of the HC-SR04
0:56 The piezo disc
1:08 How it measures (4 steps)
1:33 The maths & Arduino code
2:09 Range, beam & blind spots
2:34 Real-world uses & recap

📐 KEY FORMULAS
Distance = speed of sound × echo time ÷ 2
d (cm) = echo time (µs) ÷ 58
Speed of sound in air ≈ 343 m/s at 20 °C (≈ 331 + 0.6 × T)

🔌 HC-SR04 QUICK FACTS
• 5 V supply, about 15 mA
• 40 kHz ultrasonic burst (8 pulses)
• 10 µs trigger pulse on TRIG
• Range: about 2 cm to 4 m, beam about 15°
• Pins: VCC, TRIG, ECHO, GND

💻 ARDUINO CODE
digitalWrite(TRIG, HIGH);
delayMicroseconds(10);
digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW);
long t = pulseIn(ECHO, HIGH);
float cm = t / 58.0;

Diagrams are simplified and not to scale. Narration uses a text-to-speech voice; animation, music and sound effects are made in code.
